findings.body: The overlay mounts `./deploy/mongo/kernel-bypass-entrypoint.py` into the container and sets it as the `mongod` entrypoint, but the diff does not include or reference the script itself. If this file does not exist in the repository (or is not present on the developer's machine), `docker compose up` with this overlay will fail at the volume mount or at entrypoint execution. I could not verify the script's existence or its contents from the diff alone.
findings.title: Verify kernel-bypass-entrypoint.py exists in the repo

lookups.why: Need to see the base mongod entrypoint and command to verify the overlay's entrypoint replacement is compatible and that arguments are passed through correctly.
Determine whether the referenced Python shim exists in the repository and review its implementation.
If the script exists, verify it properly invokes mongod with passthrough arguments and does not introduce issues.

value.summary: The overlay adds a docker-compose file that replaces the mongod entrypoint with a Python shim and sets GLIBC_TUNABLES to disable rseq, with comments explaining it as a local-development workaround for MongoDB on newer Linux kernels. The approach is sound in principle, but the overlay depends on `deploy/mongo/kernel-bypass-entrypoint.py` existing in the repo — I could not verify this from the diff alone, and if it is missing the overlay will fail at runtime.
